sample_unit: chatbot responses (78 avulsion vignettes x 2 sessions)

links.outcome: Time-critical safety flag (accurate immediate action and contraindication advice) in emergency dental avulsion responses
links.effect: Safety flag present in 81% and 89% of cases across two sessions (p = 0.009), leaving roughly one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
links.quote: The safety flag was present in 81% and 89% of cases (χ<sup>2</sup> = 6.73, p = 0.009), with one in eight potentially unsafe situations.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot responses across two sessions 14 days apart
links.effect: Safety flag differed between sessions (81% vs 89%, p = 0.009), though inter-rater reproducibility was near perfect (ICC = 0.94).
links.quote: The safety flag was present in 81% and 89% of cases (χ<sup>2</sup> = 6.73, p = 0.009), with one in eight potentially unsafe situations.

unlisted_practices: guideline-linked retrieval before unsupervised deployment of emergency chatbots

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4o's performance on rewritten clinical vignettes of dental avulsion emergencies to see if it can provide accurate advice to laypersons. It evaluates model accuracy and safety without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
